clue.text: Poles close to France, scattered

parts.note: spars are poles, as on a ship's rigging

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, so take the end of France

explanation.surface: Poles living near France are thinly spread.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sparse is thinly distributed, meaning scattered here and there.

clue.text: Low pass in game

parts.note: low in volume, as a soft voice
a ball is a pass in football, as in a long ball

explanation.surface: A soft pass made during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a gentle pass within a match; in fact the last word is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This bat-and-ball sport is a variant of baseball played with a larger ball.

clue.text: Girl should squeeze in figure, one feels

indicators.note: squeeze in means one piece is pushed inside another

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name
ten is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: A girl ought to fit a number in, someone feels.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect's feeler is the organ with which it feels its way.

clue.text: Little money husband and wife entered in tax, a quarter

parts.note: a sou is a small French coin, a trifling sum

indicators.note: entered in means the pieces go inside the word for tax

parts.note: to tax someone is to test them

explanation.surface: Married couple with little cash caught up in tax over a quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the compass quarters between south and west, a quarter of the compass.

clue.text: Unimportant fellow

definitions.meaning: a question that is of no practical consequence is merely theoretical
a fellow is a university teacher or scholar

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both of purely theoretical interest and a member of a university's teaching staff.

clue.text: Drunken lord eschews inn, as ineffectual toff

indicators.note: drunken suggests staggering about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tipsy peer avoids the pub, being a feeble upper-class twit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eschews' looks like the instruction to remove letters, but every word of 'lord eschews inn' is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: This British phrase mocks a weak, foolish upper-class man, an ineffectual toff.

clue.text: Wizard showing ultimate in prestidigitation

parts.note: a demo is a showing or demonstration

indicators.note: ultimate means the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A magician displaying the best sleight of hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A demon at something is an expert, like a wizard at it.

clue.text: Against being picked up in spy glass

indicators.note: in means it goes inside the spy word

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation

indicators.note: in a down clue picked up means lifted, so the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: Opposed to being collected in a spyglass.
explanation.definitionFit: A single eyeglass worn in one eye is a glass.

clue.text: Red pen with a prominent top

parts.note: Che Guevara was a famous red, a revolutionary
a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: A red pen with a large cap.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing someone with a large bust, the upper body being prominent.

clue.text: Lose spirit, and die

definitions.meaning: to stop trying, giving up hope
to die is to yield up the soul

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both to stop trying and literally to yield up one's soul at death.

clue.text: Cook cut it fine — as it should be

definitions.text: Cook cut it fine — as it should be

indicators.note: to cook something is to fiddle or rework it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chef slices finely, the proper way to do it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' rearranges CUTITFINE. Read whole, the clue also describes the pasta, which is finely cut ribbons that are then cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: This pasta comes as thin flat ribbons, so cooking a finely cut one is exactly as it should be.

clue.text: Store filled with cold meat

indicators.note: the word for store is filled with another piece, which goes inside it

parts.note: a mine is a rich store or supply, as in a mine of information
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A larder packed with chilled cuts of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Minced meat, chopped very small, is commonly just called by this short name.

clue.text: Something poisonous about woman that no one wishes to hear

definitions.text: woman that no one wishes to hear

indicators.note: about means going round, so the poison word surrounds the woman

parts.note: bane is an old word for poison, as in henbane
she stands for a woman

explanation.surface: A toxic substance surrounding a woman nobody wants to listen to.
explanation.walkthrough: In Irish folklore this female spirit wails to foretell a death in the family, so nobody wants to hear her cry.
explanation.definitionFit: This folklore spirit is a woman whose wail portends a death, so her cry is unwelcome.

clue.text: Print line in chapter published externally

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: externally means on the outside, so the word for published wraps round the chapter

parts.note: a book that is out has been published

explanation.surface: A printed line inside a chapter that has come out.
explanation.definitionFit: A print made from a design carved into linoleum is a kind of print.

clue.text: Permission to quit

definitions.meaning: permission, as in asking a superior's consent
to quit means to depart from a place

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for permission granted and a verb meaning to go away.

clue.text: First away from work, float in breeze

indicators.note: the first letter is taken away from the word for work

parts.note: opus is Latin for a work, used of compositions
to hover is to float in the air

explanation.surface: Leaving work first, drifting in the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breeze' looks like part of the weather picture, but it is the definition: a breeze is a very easy task.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean something that is achieved with no effort at all.

clue.text: Primitive note written into different prayer

indicators.note: written into means these pieces go inside the word for different

parts.note: other means different
ur- is a prefix meaning original or primitive
fa is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An original musical note put into another kind of prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord's Prayer is known by its opening words.

clue.text: Sound, in parting with silver

indicators.note: parting with means losing, so the silver is taken out

parts.note: in means fashionable, very popular at the moment
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Healthy, in spite of giving up silver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but is the fodder: fashionable, ALL THE RAGE, which loses AG.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone of sound mind is mentally alert, the idiom for not being crazy.

clue.text: Programme with food containing things I'm surprised to eat?

indicators.note: containing means the word for food holds another piece inside it

parts.note: chow is slang for food
people say 'I'll eat my hat' about something they would be amazed to see happen

explanation.surface: A programme featuring food that includes items one would be amazed to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A television or radio programme where a host interviews guests is a type of programme.

clue.text: Worker in need of drink, given armed robber's demand

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in a farmhand
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A labourer needing a drink, faced with a gunman's order.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunman orders victims to raise their arms with this stock phrase.

clue.text: Unwanted individual sent back in disgust

indicators.note: sent back means the letters of the outcast word are written in the reverse order

parts.note: a leper is a social outcast, a person nobody wants around

explanation.surface: An unwelcome person is sent home, which causes revulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel someone is to fill them with revulsion, so it means to disgust them.

clue.text: Take it quietly, and take it up again

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly
to resume is to restart something

explanation.surface: Accept something calmly, then pick it up once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To presume is to take something for granted, to suppose it.

clue.text: Grammatical construction comes apart in speech

indicators.note: in speech means the word is spoken, giving a same-sounding one

parts.note: fabric that frays comes apart at the edges

explanation.surface: A sentence structure falls to pieces when spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of words forming a unit within a sentence is a grammatical construction.

clue.text: Execute villain, as guilty

parts.note: to hang someone is to execute them
dog is an old term for a contemptible villain

explanation.surface: Put the villain to death, since he is guilty.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangdog look is shamefaced, the expression of someone who feels guilty.

clue.text: Heading for defeat, major in terror

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to read a subject at a British university is to study it as one's main subject

explanation.surface: On the way to defeat, a senior officer in panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'major' looks like an army officer, but 'major in' is the American phrase for studying a subject, here read.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great fear, a synonym for terror.

clue.text: Given attention in the home, so touching?

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a nest is a home, as in a family nest
to give ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Being looked after at home is so moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touching' suggests emotion, but the definition plays on touching as being in contact, which is as close as can be.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are touching are as close as possible, the superlative of near.

clue.text: Part of church where wedding vow briefly spoken?

indicators.note: spoken means the shortened vow is said aloud, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: the vow I will, shortened to its contraction, is I'll

explanation.surface: Where in a church is the wedding promise quickly said?
explanation.walkthrough: The vow cut short gives I'LL, which sounds like the answer; the couple also walks up this passage at a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: The passage between the pews in a church is part of the building.

clue.text: Public assembly's welcoming situation

parts.note: open means public, available to all
a house is a legislative assembly, such as the House of Commons

explanation.surface: A public assembly's welcoming position.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping open house means being ready to receive guests at any time, a welcoming situation.

clue.text: Rush to change key on old piano

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the change-and-key pieces follow the old piano pieces

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in an ex-wife
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
to edit is to change a text
E is one of the musical keys

explanation.surface: Hurrying to modulate key on an ancient piano.
explanation.definitionFit: To expedite is to speed something up, so to rush it.

clue.text: Don't move an ornamental strip, say

indicators.note: say means the word is spoken, giving a same-sounding word

parts.note: a frieze is a decorated band along a wall

explanation.surface: Stay still, ornamental band, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay completely still is to stop moving, as when told to stay put.
